question: The three fundamental principles of radiation protection, as adopted by ICRP and AERB, are:

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: ALARA is part of the Optimisation principle, not a separate third principle. The three formal principles are Justification, Optimisation (ALARA), and Dose Limitation.

Correct. These are the three ICRP principles adopted by AERB: (1) Justification — benefit must outweigh risk; (2) Optimisation (ALARA) — dose as low as reasonably achievable; (3) Dose Limitation — individual dose must not exceed regulatory limits.
Time, distance, and shielding are the practical methods of ALARA — the tools for achieving optimisation — not the three fundamental principles themselves.
These are general safety concepts, not the formal ICRP radiation protection principles used in regulatory frameworks.

overallFeedback.feedback: Not quite. The three ICRP/AERB principles are Justification (benefit > risk), Optimisation (ALARA — keep doses as low as reasonably achievable), and Dose Limitation (individual exposure must not exceed set limits).
Correct! Justification, Optimisation (ALARA), and Dose Limitation are the three ICRP principles that form the basis of AERB regulation in India.
